- Inox Green to deploy ~INR 600 cr FY27 cash profit: first integrate 2 acquisitions, then selective GW-scale acquisitions ("≤10–20% of FCF"); limited targets left (sector consolidated: of 5 players, 2 allied, 3 bankrupt, 2 of those acquired). Dividend policy deferred until consolidation done; buyback "not at this point."
- IWEL merged into IWL (promoters cited minority-shareholder protection over their own control preference).
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
- **Guidance credibility / overcommit history** — sharply challenged by investors (megawatt→revenue metric switch, FY26 revenue miss, YoY decline vs peers doing ~40% growth). Mgmt cites force-majeure (geopolitics/shipping/ECS delay, PSU payment delay).
- **Working capital** — Q3 target of ~200 net WC days; not clearly confirmed at Q4. Whole thesis hinges on equipment-supply pivot fixing this.
- **Group-related-party dependence** — ~1/3 future execution from captive Inox Clean; large share of Inox Green "income" is acquisition/treasury-related, not core operating.
- **Execution risk** — ROW/grid-connectivity delays; majority EPC closure pushed to H1 FY27.
- **Receivables** — PSU contract delays (mgmt says resolved).
- **Acquisition closing risk** — both Inox Green acquisitions still awaiting NCLT/EOI clearances.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: - Defensive-but-assertive. Devansh Jain pushed back hard ("I beg to disagree") on value-destruction and overcommit criticism, anchoring on 4-year track record and ~$10bn renewable-arm valuation; dismissive of "short-term aberrations in market cap." Candid admission of "some failures." Tone is conviction-heavy and group-narrative-driven; investors visibly skeptical on delivery vs promises.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- The real engine is **Inox Clean (unlisted)** captive demand — minority IWL/IGESL shareholders are effectively riding a related-party order pipeline they cannot directly own.
- Reported Inox Green profitability is **materially inflated by acquisition-debt "other income"** (~INR 40 cr/qtr); core O&M margin ~45% vs headline ~50%, and quarterly revenue is lumpy (Q3 ~INR 78 cr → Q4 ~INR 69 cr).
- Company has stopped giving MW execution numbers entirely — reduces accountability/comparability vs peers.
- IRSL auto-listing is a near-term (1–2 month) value-unlock event to watch.
- "Only Indian wind player to survive with zero haircut" — sector has effectively consolidated to Inox + one rival.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Net cash balance sheet as on Mar-26", "Strong relationships with all banks" and a "Long term credit rating of AA-" are listed under the Robust Creditworthiness pillar.
- The equipment-supply pivot is explicitly a balance-sheet strategy: "The pivot is part of a larger strategy to achieve a healthy balance sheet as well as financial robustness".
- Shareholding as on June 30, 2026: Promoters 44%, Foreign Investors 15%, Domestic Institutional Investors 9%, Retail & Others 32%; "Sizeable holding of promoter group".
- The deck names investors including "Capital Research, Blackrock, ICICI Pru AMC, Bandan MF, Nippon Life India MF, Bajaj Life Insurance, PNB Metlife, Matthews, HDFC MF, Motilal Oswal MF".
- No dividend, buyback or payout policy is mentioned anywhere in the deck.

bull_bear.body:
- One of the most integrated renewable energy players in India - capabilities span project site identification, acquisition, resource assessment, manufacturing, EPC execution and long-term O&M, enabling plug-and-play execution, reducing execution risk and providing a competitive advantage over OEMs focused solely on equipment supply.
- Net-cash-positive capital structure as on Mar 26 with a long-term credit rating of AA- and the highest short-term rating of A1+, giving financial flexibility to scale with the market opportunity.
- In-house production of all critical turbine components - nacelles, hubs, blades and towers - engineered specifically for India's low wind speed regimes, giving high domestic content integration.
- Early alignment with the MNRE ALMM (Wind) framework and 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components, reducing exposure to import restrictions and supporting preferred positioning in central and state PSU tenders under Make in India.
- Technology access through long-term technology-sharing and licensing agreements with global partners such as AMSC and W2E, underpinning the 4X MW platform roadmap and LCOE optimisation.
- Scaled, geographically diversified manufacturing footprint of 2.5 GW annual capacity across five facilities in Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, de-risking supply chain and meeting domestic sourcing mandates.
- High-margin asset-light annuity O&M business through listed subsidiary IGESL, the only listed pure-play renewable O&M player in India, managing a portfolio of approximately 13.3 GWp with long-term contracts of 5 to 20 years and machine availability exceeding 95%.
- Backward integration into transformers (up to 3.5 MVA at Jaipur), an owned fleet of crawler cranes and planned power electronics, enabling faster execution, cost savings and reduced dependence on external vendors.
- Captive order visibility from Group IPP platform Inox Clean Energy, which targets 14 GW capacity by FY29 and plans to add 3 GW+ annually, of which about 20-30% is expected to be wind.
- Diversified blue-chip customer base of over 100 customers spanning PSUs (NTPC, NLC, GAIL, SJVN) and IPPs (CESC, Gentari, Hero Future Energies, Aditya Birla Group), with repeat orders reflecting execution performance.
- Resource advantage that is difficult to replicate - an extensive Meteorological (MET) mast network, a growing land bank and power evacuation infrastructure supporting project readiness.
- Over 17 years of operational experience and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed, with a strong promoter backing from the INOXGFL Group.
- Simplified corporate structure following the merger of Inox Wind Energy Limited into IWL, which eliminated the holding company structure and reduced liabilities by approximately Rs 2,050 crores, supported by a Rs 1,249 crore rights issue.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Financial risk — earnings and liquidity volatility — MD&A Risk Management and Mitigation Framework defines this as potential volatility in earnings and liquidity arising from fluctuations in interest rates, credit availability and working capital cycles. Mitigation cited: elimination of interest-bearing debt and promoter preference shares (NCRPS/NCPRPS) through a rights issue and the IWEL merger, reaching a net-cash-positive position.
- Operational and execution risk — project commissioning delays — MD&A framework: delays in project commissioning due to site readiness issues, logistical bottlenecks or infrastructure constraints impact revenue recognition timelines. Mitigated by an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes, a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility, and the demerger of the substation business into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited.
- Regulatory and policy risk — ALMM (Wind) mandates and GST changes — MD&A framework: changes in government regulations, including ALMM (Wind) mandates or revisions in GST rates, may affect sector competitiveness and project economics. Mitigated by maintaining 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components and proactive localisation of the 3 MW and upcoming 4X MW platforms.
- Technology risk — product obsolescence in low-wind regimes — MD&A framework: risk of product obsolescence or failure to meet the evolving energy yield requirements of project developers in low-wind regimes. Mitigated by long-term technology licensing with global leaders such as W2E for the 4X MW platform and continued R&D investment toward LCOE optimisation.
- Dependence on grid readiness and evacuation infrastructure — The pace of renewable capacity addition is increasingly dependent on the readiness of transmission infrastructure; delays in grid expansion relative to project commissioning may lead to curtailment risks and lower plant utilisation levels, adversely affecting project returns and operational efficiency.
- Execution constraints and infrastructure bottlenecks — RoW and land acquisition — Challenges related to transmission infrastructure, grid connectivity, right-of-way issues and land acquisition continue to affect project timelines across the sector; delays in evacuation infrastructure development and regulatory approvals remain key risks to timely execution.
- Supply chain disruption and input cost volatility — Global and domestic supply chain disruptions along with volatility in input costs continue to pose challenges to project economics; although localisation is improving supply chain resilience, availability of critical components and logistics constraints may impact execution timelines and sector margins.
- State-level variability in policy implementation — Although the overall policy environment remains supportive, implementation at the state level can vary, leading to approval delays, land access, RoW and connectivity issues; variability in regulatory execution may impact project schedules and cost structures.

- **Inox Green (O&M):** 13+ GWp portfolio, targeting largest O&M in India this year, top globally by 2030. Acquired ~6.5 GW operational wind O&M of 2 erstwhile OEMs (4.5 GW + 2 GW); consolidation pending final NCLT/EOI clearances (entity 1 order in ~2 weeks; entity 2 in 60–90 days). outlook.body:
- Strengthen technology leadership and deepen manufacturing capabilities as the stated forward priorities entering FY2026-27.

- Build a resource advantage that is difficult to replicate through an extensive Meteorological (MET) mast network, a growing land bank and power evacuation infrastructure supporting wind and solar resource assessment.
- Maintain a diversified customer portfolio across utilities, IPPs, commercial and industrial customers and Group entities to reduce concentration risk and sustain order inflows.
- Shift the order mix toward a larger share of equipment supply alongside turnkey and limited-scope EPC to improve operational flexibility and working capital efficiency.
- Preserve the net-cash balance sheet and financial flexibility to invest with confidence and pursue new opportunities.

outlook.body: Inox Wind ended FY26 with an annual manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GW across five specialised facilities. The principal capacity addition of the year was the new nacelle and hub manufacturing facility at Kalyangad/Bavla near Ahmedabad (Gujarat), which was commissioned and became fully operational during the year and whose ramp-up management identifies as a foundation for FY2026-27; the BRSR risk table states this new Gujarat facility will increase production capacity by 800 to 1,000 MW. Nacelles and hubs are made at Una (Himachal Pradesh), Bhuj (Gujarat) and the new Bavla plant, while blades and tubular towers are made at Rohika (Gujarat) and Barwani (Madhya Pradesh); blade molds at the Madhya Pradesh plant were upgraded during the year. The Company says it is working on the development of a new blade and tower manufacturing facility in South India to reduce logistical costs for regional projects. On product capacity, IWL manufactures 2 MW and 3/3.3 MW WTGs, has secured a licence for the 4 MW platform with ALMM certification under process and a targeted commercial launch of the 4.45 MW (4X) platform within the calendar year (CY2026 / FY27). Backward-integration and self-reliance investments include a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility, with higher-capacity transformer manufacturing expected to start in the current calendar year; an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes with four cranes deployed and orders placed for two more; and stated plans to enter high-value-added power electronics products such as inverters through subsidiary Inox Renewable Solutions Limited. IRSL also incorporated four wholly owned subsidiaries during the year, including Giral Bess Private Limited and Sadla Windone Private Limited. Order book stood at approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, giving execution visibility of 24-36 months.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Demand for firm clean energy is rising as the share of intermittent supply in the grid reached approximately 15% in FY26 (wind + solar), driving strong demand from discoms for reliable clean energy and more RTC / FDRE tenders.
- Wind forms about 20-30% of RTC/FDRE tenders, which management describes as strong structural momentum for wind power capacity addition in the country.
- Management expects to benefit from the growing contribution of Group Company INOX Clean Energy, whose annual capacity addition programme is projected to exceed 3 GW with wind projects accounting for 20-30% of the portfolio, creating recurring multi-year order visibility from within the Group.
- Demand is increasingly shifting towards higher-capacity turbine platforms, which management frames as the rationale for the 4.X MW development.
- Backward integration is cited as a margin lever - EBITDA growth was attributed to sustained margin expansion and the benefits of the backward integration strategy.
- The growing global emphasis on energy security and renewable self-reliance is unlocking fresh investment and reinforcing India as a leading destination for wind energy development.
- Indian policy tailwinds cited include the Government target of 100 GW installed wind capacity by 2030 within a 500 GW non-fossil goal, the GST reduction on renewable equipment from 12% to 5%, ALMM expansion, ISTS charge waivers until June 2028 and Green Energy Open Access.
- Geopolitical tensions in West Asia temporarily disrupted logistics and delayed certain ECS supplies during FY2025-26.
- Standalone operating and net profit margins improved on a higher proportion of 3.3 MW WTG sales in the sales mix together with cost optimisation, per the reasons stated for ratio variances.
- Diversified order book of approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, providing execution visibility of more than 24-36 months.
- Order book break-up as on 31 July 2026 (third-party orders only, excluding INOXGFL Group entities): 59% equipment supply and 41% turnkey.
- Balanced mix of equipment supply, equipment supply with limited scope EPC, and turnkey projects.
- Orders come from utilities, Independent Power Producers (IPPs), commercial and industrial customers and Group entities, giving a well-diversified customer base and decelerating concentration risk.
- Recurring business from marquee customers and Group companies is described as providing sustained revenue visibility and strengthening medium-term growth prospects.
- More than 100 valued customers and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed to date.

nacelles, hubs, blades and towers - engineered specifically for India's low wind speed regimes, giving high domestic content integration.|Early alignment with the MNRE ALMM (Wind) framework and 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components, reducing exposure to import restrictions and supporting preferred positioning in central and state PSU tenders under Make in India.|Technology access through long-term technology-sharing and licensing agreements with global partners such as AMSC and W2E, underpinning the 4X MW platform roadmap and LCOE optimisation.|Scaled, geographically diversified manufacturing footprint of 2.5 GW annual capacity across five facilities in Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, de-risking supply chain and meeting domestic sourcing mandates.|High-margin asset-light annuity O&M business through listed subsidiary IGESL, the only listed pure-play renewable O&M player in India, managing a portfolio of approximately 13.3 GWp with long-term contracts of 5 to 20 years and machine availability exceeding 95%.|Backward integration into transformers (up to 3.5 MVA at Jaipur), an owned fleet of crawler cranes and planned power electronics, enabling faster execution, cost savings and reduced dependence on external vendors.|Captive order visibility from Group IPP platform Inox Clean Energy, which targets 14 GW capacity by FY29 and plans to add 3 GW+ annually, of which about 20-30% is expected to be wind.|Diversified blue-chip customer base of over 100 customers spanning PSUs (NTPC, NLC, GAIL, SJVN) and IPPs (CESC, Gentari, Hero Future Energies, Aditya Birla Group), with repeat orders reflecting execution performance.|Resource advantage that is difficult to replicate - an extensive Meteorological (MET) mast network, a growing land bank and power evacuation infrastructure supporting project readiness.|Over 17 years of operational experience and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed, with a strong promoter backing from the INOXGFL Group.|Simplified corporate structure following the merger of Inox Wind Energy Limited into IWL, which eliminated the holding company structure and reduced liabilities by approximately Rs 2,050 crores, supported by a Rs 1,249 crore rights issue.
currentContext.strategies: Strengthen technology leadership and deepen manufacturing capabilities as the stated forward priorities entering FY2026-27.|Advance the product roadmap toward higher-capacity platforms - developing the 4.X MW (4.45 MW) next-generation turbine, with ALMM certification under process and commercial launch targeted within the calendar year, to broaden market opportunity and support stronger profitability.|Build manufacturing capacity as a strategic priority - the Kalyangad/Kalyangadh nacelle and hub facility near Ahmedabad was commissioned during the year and its ramp-up underpins the year ahead.|Pursue backward integration and strategic self-reliance - start manufacturing higher-capacity transformers this calendar year, operate an in-house crane fleet (four deployed, two more on order), and enter high value added power electronics products.|Operate a fully integrated end-to-end renewable platform combining wind turbine manufacturing, renewable infrastructure development, EPC and O&M, delivered through specialised Group entities.|Build a resource advantage that is difficult to replicate through an extensive Meteorological (MET) mast network, a growing land bank and power evacuation infrastructure supporting wind and solar resource assessment.|Maintain a diversified customer portfolio across utilities, IPPs, commercial and industrial customers and Group entities to reduce concentration risk and sustain order inflows.|Shift the order mix toward a larger share of equipment supply alongside turnkey and limited-scope EPC to improve operational flexibility and working capital efficiency.|Preserve the net-cash balance sheet and financial flexibility to invest with confidence and pursue new opportunities.|Maintain 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components and localise the 3 MW and upcoming 4X MW platforms to comply early with ALMM (Wind) requirements.
currentContext.expansion: Inox Wind ended FY26 with an annual manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GW across five specialised facilities. The principal capacity addition of the year was the new nacelle and hub manufacturing facility at Kalyangad/Bavla near Ahmedabad (Gujarat), which was commissioned and became fully operational during the year and whose ramp-up management identifies as a foundation for FY2026-27; the BRSR risk table states this new Gujarat facility will increase production capacity by 800 to 1,000 MW. Nacelles and hubs are made at Una (Himachal Pradesh), Bhuj (Gujarat) and the new Bavla plant, while blades and tubular towers are made at Rohika (Gujarat) and Barwani (Madhya Pradesh); blade molds at the Madhya Pradesh plant were upgraded during the year. The Company says it is working on the development of a new blade and tower manufacturing facility in South India to reduce logistical costs for regional projects. On product capacity, IWL manufactures 2 MW and 3/3.3 MW WTGs, has secured a licence for the 4 MW platform with ALMM certification under process and a targeted commercial launch of the 4.45 MW (4X) platform within the calendar year (CY2026 / FY27). Backward-integration and self-reliance investments include a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility, with higher-capacity transformer manufacturing expected to start in the current calendar year; an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes with four cranes deployed and orders placed for two more; and stated plans to enter high-value-added power electronics products such as inverters through subsidiary Inox Renewable Solutions Limited. IRSL also incorporated four wholly owned subsidiaries during the year, including Giral Bess Private Limited and Sadla Windone Private Limited. Order book stood at approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, giving execution visibility of 24-36 months.
currentContext.mdna: Demand for firm clean energy is rising as the share of intermittent supply in the grid reached approximately 15% in FY26 (wind + solar), driving strong demand from discoms for reliable clean energy and more RTC / FDRE tenders.|Wind forms about 20-30% of RTC/FDRE tenders, which management describes as strong structural momentum for wind power capacity addition in the country.|Management expects to benefit from the growing contribution of Group Company INOX Clean Energy, whose annual capacity addition programme is projected to exceed 3 GW with wind projects accounting for 20-30% of the portfolio, creating recurring multi-year order visibility from within the Group.|Demand is increasingly shifting towards higher-capacity turbine platforms, which management frames as the rationale for the 4.X MW development.|Backward integration is cited as a margin lever - EBITDA growth was attributed to sustained margin expansion and the benefits of the backward integration strategy.|The growing global emphasis on energy security and renewable self-reliance is unlocking fresh investment and reinforcing India as a leading destination for wind energy development.|Indian policy tailwinds cited include the Government target of 100 GW installed wind capacity by 2030 within a 500 GW non-fossil goal, the GST reduction on renewable equipment from 12% to 5%, ALMM expansion, ISTS charge waivers until June 2028 and Green Energy Open Access.|Geopolitical tensions in West Asia temporarily disrupted logistics and delayed certain ECS supplies during FY2025-26.|Standalone operating and net profit margins improved on a higher proportion of 3.3 MW WTG sales in the sales mix together with cost optimisation, per the reasons stated for ratio variances.|Diversified order book of approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, providing execution visibility of more than 24-36 months.|Order book break-up as on 31 July 2026 (third-party orders only, excluding INOXGFL Group entities): 59% equipment supply and 41% turnkey.|Balanced mix of equipment supply, equipment supply with limited scope EPC, and turnkey projects.|Orders come from utilities, Independent Power Producers (IPPs), commercial and industrial customers and Group entities, giving a well-diversified customer base and decelerating concentration risk.|Recurring business from marquee customers and Group companies is described as providing sustained revenue visibility and strengthening medium-term growth prospects.|More than 100 valued customers and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed to date.

risks.risk: Financial risk — earnings and liquidity volatility
risks.note: MD&A Risk Management and Mitigation Framework defines this as potential volatility in earnings and liquidity arising from fluctuations in interest rates, credit availability and working capital cycles. Mitigation cited: elimination of interest-bearing debt and promoter preference shares (NCRPS/NCPRPS) through a rights issue and the IWEL merger, reaching a net-cash-positive position.

risks.risk: Operational and execution risk — project commissioning delays
risks.note: MD&A framework: delays in project commissioning due to site readiness issues, logistical bottlenecks or infrastructure constraints impact revenue recognition timelines. Mitigated by an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes, a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility, and the demerger of the substation business into Inox Renewable Solutions Limited.

risks.risk: Regulatory and policy risk — ALMM (Wind) mandates and GST changes
risks.note: MD&A framework: changes in government regulations, including ALMM (Wind) mandates or revisions in GST rates, may affect sector competitiveness and project economics. Mitigated by maintaining 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components and proactive localisation of the 3 MW and upcoming 4X MW platforms.

risks.risk: Technology risk — product obsolescence in low-wind regimes
risks.note: MD&A framework: risk of product obsolescence or failure to meet the evolving energy yield requirements of project developers in low-wind regimes. Mitigated by long-term technology licensing with global leaders such as W2E for the 4X MW platform and continued R&D investment toward LCOE optimisation.

risks.risk: Dependence on grid readiness and evacuation infrastructure
risks.note: The pace of renewable capacity addition is increasingly dependent on the readiness of transmission infrastructure; delays in grid expansion relative to project commissioning may lead to curtailment risks and lower plant utilisation levels, adversely affecting project returns and operational efficiency.

risks.risk: Execution constraints and infrastructure bottlenecks — RoW and land acquisition
risks.note: Challenges related to transmission infrastructure, grid connectivity, right-of-way issues and land acquisition continue to affect project timelines across the sector; delays in evacuation infrastructure development and regulatory approvals remain key risks to timely execution.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption and input cost volatility
risks.note: Global and domestic supply chain disruptions along with volatility in input costs continue to pose challenges to project economics; although localisation is improving supply chain resilience, availability of critical components and logistics constraints may impact execution timelines and sector margins.

Although the overall policy environment remains supportive, implementation at the state level can vary, leading to approval delays, land access, RoW and connectivity issues; variability in regulatory execution may impact project schedules and cost structures.

- IRSL listing as a value-unlock catalyst.

- Rising O&M mix (50% margin business) biases blended margin higher.
- Backward integration (cranes ~50% in-house → fully in-house this year; transformers ramping) supports margins/liquidity.

- IWEL merged into IWL (promoters cited minority-shareholder protection over their own control preference).
risks & watch-items:
- **Guidance credibility / overcommit history** — sharply challenged by investors (megawatt→revenue metric switch, FY26 revenue miss, YoY decline vs peers doing ~40% growth). Mgmt cites force-majeure (geopolitics/shipping/ECS delay, PSU payment delay).
- **Working capital** — Q3 target of ~200 net WC days; not clearly confirmed at Q4. Whole thesis hinges on equipment-supply pivot fixing this.
- **Group-related-party dependence** — ~1/3 future execution from captive Inox Clean; large share of Inox Green "income" is acquisition/treasury-related, not core operating.
- **Execution risk** — ROW/grid-connectivity delays; majority EPC closure pushed to H1 FY27.
- **Receivables** — PSU contract delays (mgmt says resolved).
- **Acquisition closing risk** — both Inox Green acquisitions still awaiting NCLT/EOI clearances.

Devansh Jain pushed back hard ("I beg to disagree") on value-destruction and overcommit criticism, anchoring on 4-year track record and ~$10bn renewable-arm valuation; dismissive of "short-term aberrations in market cap." Candid admission of "some failures." Tone is conviction-heavy and group-narrative-driven; investors visibly skeptical on delivery vs promises.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The real engine is **Inox Clean (unlisted)** captive demand — minority IWL/IGESL shareholders are effectively riding a related-party order pipeline they cannot directly own.
- Reported Inox Green profitability is **materially inflated by acquisition-debt "other income"** (~INR 40 cr/qtr); core O&M margin ~45% vs headline ~50%, and quarterly revenue is lumpy (Q3 ~INR 78 cr → Q4 ~INR 69 cr).

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Inox Wind Limited is one of India's leading fully integrated wind energy solution providers, an INOXGFL Group company delivering end-to-end solutions across project development, manufacturing, execution and long-term O&M, with a manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GW.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: Inox Wind manufactures Wind Turbine Generators and their critical components - nacelles, hubs, blades and tubular towers - designed specifically for India's low wind speed regimes, and supplies them alongside end-to-end wind energy solutions covering site identification and acquisition, resource assessment, EPC execution and long-term operations and maintenance. Its customers are independent power producers, public sector undertakings and a diverse portfolio of commercial and industrial clients, all in the domestic Indian market. Manufacturing accounts for about 95% of turnover and sale of services about 5%, with subsidiary Inox Green Energy Services Limited providing renewable O&M and subsidiary Inox Renewable Solutions Limited providing turnkey and limited-scope EPC, crane services and transformer manufacturing.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Demand for firm clean energy is rising as the share of intermittent supply in the grid reached approximately 15% in FY26 (wind + solar), driving strong demand from discoms for reliable clean energy and more RTC / FDRE tenders.
- Wind forms about 20-30% of RTC/FDRE tenders, which management describes as strong structural momentum for wind power capacity addition in the country.
- Management expects to benefit from the growing contribution of Group Company INOX Clean Energy, whose annual capacity addition programme is projected to exceed 3 GW with wind projects accounting for 20-30% of the portfolio, creating recurring multi-year order visibility from within the Group.
- Demand is increasingly shifting towards higher-capacity turbine platforms, which management frames as the rationale for the 4.X MW development.
- Backward integration is cited as a margin lever - EBITDA growth was attributed to sustained margin expansion and the benefits of the backward integration strategy.
- The growing global emphasis on energy security and renewable self-reliance is unlocking fresh investment and reinforcing India as a leading destination for wind energy development.
- Indian policy tailwinds cited include the Government target of 100 GW installed wind capacity by 2030 within a 500 GW non-fossil goal, the GST reduction on renewable equipment from 12% to 5%, ALMM expansion, ISTS charge waivers until June 2028 and Green Energy Open Access.
- Geopolitical tensions in West Asia temporarily disrupted logistics and delayed certain ECS supplies during FY2025-26.
- Standalone operating and net profit margins improved on a higher proportion of 3.3 MW WTG sales in the sales mix together with cost optimisation, per the reasons stated for ratio variances.
- Diversified order book of approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, providing execution visibility of more than 24-36 months.
- Order book break-up as on 31 July 2026 (third-party orders only, excluding INOXGFL Group entities): 59% equipment supply and 41% turnkey.
- Balanced mix of equipment supply, equipment supply with limited scope EPC, and turnkey projects.
- Orders come from utilities, Independent Power Producers (IPPs), commercial and industrial customers and Group entities, giving a well-diversified customer base and decelerating concentration risk.
- Recurring business from marquee customers and Group companies is described as providing sustained revenue visibility and strengthening medium-term growth prospects.
- More than 100 valued customers and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed to date.

margins.body:

- Rising O&M mix (50% margin business) biases blended margin higher.
- Backward integration (cranes ~50% in-house → fully in-house this year; transformers ramping) supports margins/liquidity.

Dividend policy deferred until consolidation done; buyback "not at this point."

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Inox Wind ended FY26 with an annual manufacturing capacity of 2.5 GW across five specialised facilities. The principal capacity addition of the year was the new nacelle and hub manufacturing facility at Kalyangad/Bavla near Ahmedabad (Gujarat), which was commissioned and became fully operational during the year and whose ramp-up management identifies as a foundation for FY2026-27; the BRSR risk table states this new Gujarat facility will increase production capacity by 800 to 1,000 MW. Nacelles and hubs are made at Una (Himachal Pradesh), Bhuj (Gujarat) and the new Bavla plant, while blades and tubular towers are made at Rohika (Gujarat) and Barwani (Madhya Pradesh); blade molds at the Madhya Pradesh plant were upgraded during the year. The Company says it is working on the development of a new blade and tower manufacturing facility in South India to reduce logistical costs for regional projects. On product capacity, IWL manufactures 2 MW and 3/3.3 MW WTGs, has secured a licence for the 4 MW platform with ALMM certification under process and a targeted commercial launch of the 4.45 MW (4X) platform within the calendar year (CY2026 / FY27). Backward-integration and self-reliance investments include a dedicated transformer manufacturing facility, with higher-capacity transformer manufacturing expected to start in the current calendar year; an in-house fleet of 750-ton crawler cranes with four cranes deployed and orders placed for two more; and stated plans to enter high-value-added power electronics products such as inverters through subsidiary Inox Renewable Solutions Limited. IRSL also incorporated four wholly owned subsidiaries during the year, including Giral Bess Private Limited and Sadla Windone Private Limited. Order book stood at approximately 4.4 GW as on July 2026, giving execution visibility of 24-36 months.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: - Defensive-but-assertive. Devansh Jain pushed back hard ("I beg to disagree") on value-destruction and overcommit criticism, anchoring on 4-year track record and ~$10bn renewable-arm valuation; dismissive of "short-term aberrations in market cap." Candid admission of "some failures." Tone is conviction-heavy and group-narrative-driven; investors visibly skeptical on delivery vs promises.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- One of the most integrated renewable energy players in India - capabilities span project site identification, acquisition, resource assessment, manufacturing, EPC execution and long-term O&M, enabling plug-and-play execution, reducing execution risk and providing a competitive advantage over OEMs focused solely on equipment supply.
- Net-cash-positive capital structure as on Mar 26 with a long-term credit rating of AA- and the highest short-term rating of A1+, giving financial flexibility to scale with the market opportunity.
- In-house production of all critical turbine components - nacelles, hubs, blades and towers - engineered specifically for India's low wind speed regimes, giving high domestic content integration.
- Early alignment with the MNRE ALMM (Wind) framework and 75-80% domestic sourcing of critical components, reducing exposure to import restrictions and supporting preferred positioning in central and state PSU tenders under Make in India.
- Technology access through long-term technology-sharing and licensing agreements with global partners such as AMSC and W2E, underpinning the 4X MW platform roadmap and LCOE optimisation.
- Scaled, geographically diversified manufacturing footprint of 2.5 GW annual capacity across five facilities in Himachal Pradesh, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh, de-risking supply chain and meeting domestic sourcing mandates.
- High-margin asset-light annuity O&M business through listed subsidiary IGESL, the only listed pure-play renewable O&M player in India, managing a portfolio of approximately 13.3 GWp with long-term contracts of 5 to 20 years and machine availability exceeding 95%.
- Backward integration into transformers (up to 3.5 MVA at Jaipur), an owned fleet of crawler cranes and planned power electronics, enabling faster execution, cost savings and reduced dependence on external vendors.
- Captive order visibility from Group IPP platform Inox Clean Energy, which targets 14 GW capacity by FY29 and plans to add 3 GW+ annually, of which about 20-30% is expected to be wind.
- Diversified blue-chip customer base of over 100 customers spanning PSUs (NTPC, NLC, GAIL, SJVN) and IPPs (CESC, Gentari, Hero Future Energies, Aditya Birla Group), with repeat orders reflecting execution performance.
- Resource advantage that is difficult to replicate - an extensive Meteorological (MET) mast network, a growing land bank and power evacuation infrastructure supporting project readiness.
- Over 17 years of operational experience and approximately 3.4 GW of projects executed, with a strong promoter backing from the INOXGFL Group.
- Simplified corporate structure following the merger of Inox Wind Energy Limited into IWL, which eliminated the holding company structure and reduced liabilities by approximately Rs 2,050 crores, supported by a Rs 1,249 crore rights issue.

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Guidance credibility / overcommit history** — sharply challenged by investors (megawatt→revenue metric switch, FY26 revenue miss, YoY decline vs peers doing ~40% growth). Mgmt cites force-majeure (geopolitics/shipping/ECS delay, PSU payment delay).
- **Working capital** — Q3 target of ~200 net WC days; not clearly confirmed at Q4. Whole thesis hinges on equipment-supply pivot fixing this.
- **Group-related-party dependence** — ~1/3 future execution from captive Inox Clean; large share of Inox Green "income" is acquisition/treasury-related, not core operating.
- **Execution risk** — ROW/grid-connectivity delays; majority EPC closure pushed to H1 FY27.
- **Receivables** — PSU contract delays (mgmt says resolved).
- **Acquisition closing risk** — both Inox Green acquisitions still awaiting NCLT/EOI clearances.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The real engine is **Inox Clean (unlisted)** captive demand — minority IWL/IGESL shareholders are effectively riding a related-party order pipeline they cannot directly own.
- Reported Inox Green profitability is **materially inflated by acquisition-debt "other income"** (~INR 40 cr/qtr); core O&M margin ~45% vs headline ~50%, and quarterly revenue is lumpy (Q3 ~INR 78 cr → Q4 ~INR 69 cr).
- Company has stopped giving MW execution numbers entirely — reduces accountability/comparability vs peers.
- IRSL auto-listing is a near-term (1–2 month) value-unlock event to watch.
- "Only Indian wind player to survive with zero haircut" — sector has effectively consolidated to Inox + one rival.
